Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Persistent latency during integration test + request for remediation credit

Hi Priyom,

We ran the final integration load test yesterday (10/18) and saw repeated sustained 95th-pct latency spikes (1.2–1.6s) across multiple endpoints between 13:40–14:10 PT. This severely impacted our demo cohort and downstream data pipelines.

This is blocking our go-live target for mid-November. Our procurement team is asking for a remediation path plus an interim commercial concession while you stabilize the service. Specifically, they want either: 
- one month of service credit (full account waiver for Nov), or
- a structured partial credit (25% off Oct invoice) plus guaranteed remediation milestones with weekly status.

Please let me know what you can commit to this morning — the execs are waiting.

Attaching our basic impact snapshot.

Thanks,
Julia Barnes
Director of Integrations, Aperture AI

Folks — forwarding Aperture's ask. Short version: serious 95th-pct latency during their integration test; they're threatening to delay Nov go-live and want an interim credit.

Proposed commercial options (my thinking):
1) Conditional abatement: 2 free service weeks (applied to Nov invoice) if we hit the remediation milestones (see attached SLO plan).
2) Financial partial: 25% credit on Oct invoice, with mandatory weekly ops sync + commit to the remediation schedule.

I prefer option 1 tied to remediation because it preserves goodwill without immediate cash impact; we can also offer a $15k marketing co-op credit (in addition) that Aperture could apply to co-marketing.

Asking for exec sign-off if the total value exceeds $40k equivalent (finance threshold). Attaching impact analysis + a proposed credit schedule.

Attachments: slo-impact-analysis.pdf, proposed-credit-schedule.csv

—Priyom
Priyom Das

Priyom — thanks for the write-up. A few quick questions before we escalate to Exec Approval Committee:
1) What is the estimated $ value of the proposed two-week credit + marketing co-op? (need a number)
2) Do we have logs that show root cause is on our side (not customer config)? If not, put that in the remediation plan — legal will push back if it's ambiguous.
3) Is there any contractual SLO breach already triggered per the signed MSA? If yes, show how this maps to the SLO clauses.

If the total concession (credit + co-op) is >$40k, we need a 2-signer approval (Sales + Finance). Jonas, can you prelim math? Lauren, quick check on amendment language — we want the credit to be conditional and timeboxed; no permanency to price.

If we can keep this as a 2-week credit conditional on milestones, I'm inclined to approve to preserve the go-live. But I want the documents cleaned up before giving formal sign-off.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

- Two-week service credit = estimated $34,200 (based on their committed consumption run-rate).
- Marketing co-op credit (one-time) = $6,000.
- Total effective concession = $40,200 (just over the $40k threshold).

- Credit applied only if our canary passes and we show no repeat incidents for 14 days.
- Aperture signs a short amendment that documents the conditional credit and remediation milestones (DocuSign link below).
- Finance to process credit only after verification by Ops.

1) The credit is limited to two service weeks (value capped at $34,200) plus the $6k marketing credit — total not to exceed $40,200.

4) Finance (jonas) to issue credit and record as a one-time concession; do not change list pricing.

Jonas — please run the credit memo and confirm accounting treatment. Lauren — please push the DocuSign amendment; Priyom, ensure Aperture signs prior to credit issuance.
